title: poc-final-synthesis-deploy-options-and-playbook
body:
Executive summary:

This document synthesizes findings from the two-week Atlas FinServ POC, summarizes technical and business signals from the workshop with the customer, and presents three deployment options with an actionable playbook for the recommended path. The POC validated model quality on typical FinServ prompts, demonstrated end-to-end latency under light load, and surfaced two integration risk areas: KV cache sizing under long-conversation scenarios and cross-region failure handover for private deployments.

POC context and objectives:
- Customer: Atlas Financial Services (small to mid-sized banking platform).
- Primary objectives: (1) Validate Redwood hosted API can meet 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for single-turn scoring at median token lengths, (2) Confirm hallucination rate on compliance prompts is below 3% per our eval criteria, (3) Evaluate options for a private deployment behind Atlas VPC with KMS integration.
- Duration: 2025-01-20 to 2025-02-03 (2 weeks active testing + workshop).
- Test surfaces: batch scoring engine, interactive agent flows, and embeddings-based search.

Key metrics and outcomes (quantitative):
- Latency: 95th percentile single-turn generation (hosted) = 270ms; median = 120ms (measured over 2k mixed prompts).
- Throughput: Sustained throughput on dedicated medium pool equivalent = ~450 tokens/s per GPU for the model variant used.
- Quality: Compliance prompt hallucination rate = 2.1% (spot-checked against human-labeled gold set).
- Cost signal: Hosted per-token estimate at expected scale (100M tokens/month) = projected $12k/month before discounts; dedicated reserved capacity model reduces token-cost-equivalent by ~28% for the measured workload shape.

Technical findings and notes from the workshop:
1) Model variant fit:
   - The quantized 8-bit variant preserved quality on compliance prompts while reducing memory pressure. We recommend this as the baseline for Dedicated/Private deployments.
2) KV cache sizing and long conversations:
   - In long-chat stress tests (>8k combined context), KV cache eviction caused repeated re-encoding and latency spikes. Root cause: default cache capacity tuned for 4–6k contexts.
   - Short-term mitigation: increase cache allocation per shard and enable prefix caching for known system prompts.
   - Long-term: workload-aware dynamic cache expansion and eviction policy is an ops item for runtime team.
3) Private deployment integration:
   - KMS integration via Atlas HSM completed in workshop; however, audit-log forwarding required a custom shim to satisfy their SIEM format (workaround documented in linked artifacts).
4) Cross-region failover:
   - We exercised policy-based failover using smart-routing fallback to nearby region; warm-up times during cold start were ~1.2s for a new model container. Recommendation: maintain minimal warm pool for critical routes (<5% capacity) to ensure <500ms tail latency under failover.

Deployment options (tradeoffs):
Option A — Hosted (fastest time-to-value):
- Description: Continue on Redwood hosted API; use model variant M-8q baseline with API-level caching.
- Pros: minimal ops, fastest rollout, Redwood handles autoscaling and kernel selection.
- Cons: data residency constraints for certain Atlas customers; higher per-token cost at scale.
- Ideal for: pilot expansion and internal-facing features.

Option B — Dedicated Reserved Capacity (recommended near-term):
- Description: Dedicated GPU pools in Redwood-managed infra, reserved monthly commit. Use M-8q variant, increased KV cache per shard, and a configured warm pool for critical routes.
- Pros: predictable performance and cost, easier compliance than hosted, faster than private.
- Cons: still outside customer VPC; requires contract for reserved capacity.
- Cost: ~28% lower cost-per-token compared to hosted for projected 100M tokens/month.
- Rollout window: 4–6 weeks (contract + infra provisioning + canary).

Option C — Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS (long-term):
- Description: Private control plane, service nodes in Atlas VPC, direct KMS/HSM integration, audit-forwarding shim.
- Pros: full data residency, meets strict compliance; single-tenant isolation.
- Cons: longer lead time, higher engineering lift, we recommend for regulated production segments only.
- Rollout window: 10–14 weeks (networking, air-gapped packaging if required, validation).

Recommendation and justification:
- Short-term recommendation: pursue Option B (Dedicated Reserved Capacity) as the primary path for the next 90 days. Rationale: balances performance, cost, and speed to market; addresses most of Atlas’ compliance needs without the lead time of Private. Use Hosted only for internal pilots and experiments.
- Parallel workstream: begin Private deployment scoping and security review with Atlas’ infra team to produce a timeline and SOW for a Q3 proof-of-concept if their regulated customers require it.

Actionable playbook (90-day timeline):
Weeks 0–2 (green light):
- Contract: finalize Dedicated reserved capacity terms and expected commit (GTM/legal). Owner: Sales (Arjun).
- Infra: provision dedicated medium pool with M-8q images and +25% KV cache allocation. Owner: Infra (Samir).
- Integration: configure KMS handshake for staging, enable audit shim in a sandbox. Owner: Solutions (Maya).

Weeks 3–6 (canary + validation):
- Canary: route 2% traffic from Atlas staging to Dedicated pools; monitor latency, error rate, and hallucination metrics. Owner: SRE (Lena) + Atlas dev lead.
- Telemetry: add per-route quality checks and token-level cost dashboards; create automatic rollback policy if hallucination >3.5% or 95p latency >350ms. Owner: Observability (Elena).

Weeks 7–12 (ramp + SLA):
- Ramp: increase traffic to 60% then 100% with step-based load. Confirm warm-pool sizing meets failover targets.
- SLA: finalize SLA terms and runbook for cross-region failover. Owner: Customer Success + SRE.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: KV cache eviction causing latency spikes on long-convo flows. Mitigation: +25% cache, prefix caching, and staged rollout to monitor.
- Risk: SIEM/audit format mismatch. Mitigation: ship audit-forwarding shim and include conversion tests in canary.
- Risk: Unexpected token cost growth. Mitigation: set quota and alerting on per-route token burn; adopt intelligent batching for batch scoring flows.

Open questions for Atlas stakeholders (required answers before contract signature):
1) Desired RPO/RTO for private VPC failover scenarios?
2) Which customer segments require on-premise/private versus hosted/dedicated?
3) Acceptance criteria for hallucination tests (sample size and labeling process).

Appendix: workshop notes and quick checklist:
- Workshop reminders: include a short demo script that highlights KV cache effects on an 8k conversation.
- Pre-launch checklist:
  - [ ] Contract signed for Dedicated capacity
  - [ ] Staging KMS handshake validated
  - [ ] Canary telemetry dashboards created and shared
  - [ ] Warm pool configured (min 5% capacity)
  - [ ] Audit-forwarding shim deployed to staging
  - [ ] Rolling deploy + rollback tested

Contact and owners summary:
- POC lead / primary author: Maya Chen (solutions-engineering)
- Sales lead: Arjun Patel
- Infra/SRE: Samir Kapoor, Lena Morales
- Observability: Elena Rossi

Next immediate steps (this week):
1) Sales to send a draft Dedicated commitment and start contract review. (Owner: Arjun)
2) Infra to provision a staging Dedicated pool with M-8q and increased KV cache. (Owner: Samir)
3) Solutions to complete KMS handshake tests and provide audit shim notes to Atlas. (Owner: Maya)
4) Observability to create the hallucination, latency, and cost dashboards and set alerts. (Owner: Elena)

If approved, we will schedule the two-week canary phase kickoff meeting and share a public-facing one-pager summarizing this recommendation for Atlas execs.

Notes to self / internal reminders: keep detailed token-cost logs for the first month post-ramp; collect 500 labeled compliance prompts from Atlas for continuous quality monitoring.
